title: Bug — prevent a provider-disabled Vaporize install from breaking the Swiftly swift proxy
description: On this host, the installed Vaporize compatibility build omitted its embedded Swiftly provider but was registered as ~/.swiftly/bin/swift. Consequently, bare `swift --version` terminated with `toolchain-selection requires a provider compiled for this host: Swiftly`. Swiftly's global default also named a removed 6.4 snapshot. Installing Swift 6.3.3 and selecting it as the global default restored ~/.swiftly/bin/swift to the Swiftly proxy and made bare Swift work, but the installed Vaporize capability/proxy mismatch remains a product defect. The existing BUG-VAPORIZE-XCODE27-SWIFTLY-INPUT-PROTOCOL-2026-08-17 tracks the upstream compile cause; this Bead tracks the installed-runtime safety contract.
actualBehavior: A provider-disabled installed Vaporize binary can occupy Swiftly's `swift` proxy path, making the default Swift command unusable. Its help reports that the optional Swiftly provider is omitted, while its proxy invocation fails before reaching a selected toolchain.
expectedBehavior: A Vaporize installation without an embedded Swiftly provider must not become the active Swiftly `swift` proxy. When Vaporize owns that proxy, its embedded selection provider must be present and the selected toolchain must resolve successfully.
acceptanceCriteria: The installed-runtime installer records whether the Vaporize build contains the Swiftly provider before it can be registered as a Swiftly command proxy.
A provider-disabled compatibility build cannot replace ~/.swiftly/bin/swift; direct Swiftly proxy behavior remains intact.
An installed Vaporize build that owns the proxy proves `vaporize toolchain-selection swift -- use` and `swift --version` against an installed selected toolchain.
A regression test covers both provider-enabled and provider-disabled installation outcomes without relying on pre-existing user toolchain state.

The repair links or closes only after the Xcode 27 InputProtocol compatibility Bead and installed-runtime parity evidence identify a build with the provider restored or a safe non-proxy installation mode.
